{{Use British English|date=January 2018}}

'''David John Candlin''' (1928 in [[Croydon]], [[Surrey]]<ref>[http://search.findmypast.co.uk/results/world-records/england-and-wales-births-1837-2006?firstname=david%20j&lastname=candlin&eventyear=1928&eventyear_offset=0 Birth record]</ref> – 4 December 2019<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/scotsman-uk/obituary.aspx?pid=194664164 | title=David John Candlin | author=The Scotsman | via=legacy.com | date=9 December 2019 | accessdate=27 June 2021 }}</ref>) was an English [[physicist]]. He was known for developing the path integral formulation of the [[Fermion|Fermionic field]], inventing [[Berezin integral|Grassmann integration]] for this purpose.<ref>{{cite journal|journal= Nuovo Cimento | author= D.J. Candlin | volume =4 | title = On Sums over Trajectories for Systems With Fermi Statistics|year=1956| issue= 2 |pages=231–239|doi= 10.1007/BF02745446|bibcode=1956NCim....4..231C| s2cid= 122333001 }}</ref>  He received his PhD from [[Cambridge University]]  in 1955, and wrote his influential paper on Grassmann integration shortly thereafter.  He was later appointed a lecturer at the [[University of Edinburgh]]<ref>A Community of Scholars: The Institute for Advanced Study, Faculty and Members 1930-1980</ref> and retired from this post in 1995.<ref>[https://www.ias.edu/scholars/david-john-candlin Institute for Advanced Study]</ref> He was at one time involved in collaborative work related to [[CERN]].<ref>[https://cds.cern.ch/record/205899/files/199003601.pdf Aleph collaboration]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/GRAPHICS/Texts/Upgrade99/1999.12.01.html |title=Atlas Graphics Design |access-date=23 May 2016 |archive-date=2 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102181833/http://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/GRAPHICS/Texts/Upgrade99/1999.12.01.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/SOFTWARE/INFO/Dig/9707/arve-djc.txt |title=Atlas discussion |access-date=23 May 2016 |archive-date=2 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102074037/http://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/SOFTWARE/INFO/Dig/9707/arve-djc.txt |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://inspirehep.net/author/profile/D.J.Candlin.1 Inspire author profile for Candlin, D.J.]</ref>

In 1955 he married [[Rosemary Shaw]], crystallographer and later computer scientist.<ref>''The Times'', 6 Sep 1955, p1</ref>
